review.tagline: Removes refusal behavior from transformer language models via automated abliteration
review.summary: Heretic applies directional ablation (abliteration) to the attention out-projection and MLP down-projection matrices of a transformer model. An Optuna TPE optimizer searches the ablation parameters, co-minimizing refusals and KL divergence from the original model. After a run it can save the model, upload it to Hugging Face, chat with it, or run benchmarks.
review.audience: Users who want to decensor open-weight LLMs without manual abliteration work
strengths: One command, no configuration needed; Optuna TPE tunes ablation parameters automatically
README reports 3/100 refusals at 0.16 KL on gemma-3-12b-it, versus 0.45 and 1.04 for manual abliterations
Supports most dense models, several MoE architectures, and some multimodal and hybrid models
Optional bitsandbytes 4-bit quantization (bnb_4bit) reduces VRAM needs
weaknesses: Pure state-space models and some research architectures are not supported out of the box
AGPL-3.0 license may restrict use in proprietary or networked products
About 20-30 minutes for a 4B model on an RTX 3090; larger models unknown
README metrics come from one RTX 5090 setup and may vary by hardware
needs: Needs Python 3.10+, PyTorch 2.2+, Optuna, bitsandbytes (optional), Hugging Face
Models: Hugging Face transformer models (dense), MoE, multimodal, hybrid (Qwen3.5), MXFP4 (gpt-oss, needs PyTorch 2.6+)
